title: They Mined Bitcoin on a Nuclear Weapons Supercomputer ☢️
lesson: Side money on a work computer is never secret. Someone is always watching.
description:
Sarov, Russia: a closed city home to Russia's Federal Nuclear Center, where the first Soviet atomic bomb was built. In February 2018, engineers used the lab's one-petaflop supercomputer to mine crypto and were caught when they connected it to the internet. The institute called it "a hopeless and criminal offense." In 2019 one engineer was fined 450,000 rubles (about $7,000).

Not financial advice. Entertainment and education only.
pinned: Worst place ever to mine bitcoin? 😂 👇

scenes.line: They used a nuclear weapons supercomputer… to mine bitcoin.
Sarov, Russia. A closed city that doesn't appear on maps.
This is where the Soviet Union built its first atomic bomb. Today, it still works on nuclear warheads.
Inside: a supercomputer with one petaflop of power. A million billion calculations every second.
February 2018. Bitcoin had touched almost 20,000 dollars two months earlier.
And a few engineers get an idea. They quietly put the supercomputer to work mining bitcoin.
One problem. Mining needs the internet. And a nuclear weapons lab is supposed to stay offline.
The moment they connect it… security sees everything. Russia's security service, the FSB, walks in.
